lessons.title: What is Kotlin?
lessons.summary: The language that makes web pages interactive.

blocks.text: What is Kotlin?
Kotlin (JS) is the programming language of the web. Kotlin gives structure, skills gives style, and Kotlin gives behaviour — clicks, data, animation, and logic.
JS runs in every browser and, via Node.js, on servers too. It is dynamically typed (you don't declare types) and runs line by line.
You can run JS instantly: open your browser, press F12, and type in the Console.

items: HTML = structure, CSS = style, JS = behaviour.
JS runs in browsers and on servers (Node.js).
The browser Console is your fastest playground.

items.q: Where can JS run besides the browser?
items.explain: Node.js runs JS outside the browser.

lessons.title: Variables: let, const, var
lessons.summary: Storing values you can name and reuse.

blocks.text: Variables: let, const, var
Variables are labelled boxes for data. Modern Kotlin uses let (reassignable) and const (fixed). Avoid var — it has confusing scoping rules.
Use const by default; switch to let only when you must reassign. This makes code safer and easier to read.

items.def: A binding that cannot be reassigned.
Legacy, function-scoped — avoid in new code.

items.q: Which should you reach for by default?
items.explain: const unless you need to reassign.

blocks.text: Data Types
Kotlin has a small set of primitive types plus objects. Knowing them prevents subtle bugs.
Primitives: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, bigint, symbol. Everything else (arrays, functions) is an object.
typeof tells you a value's type at runtime.

items.explain: A historic JS bug kept for compatibility.

blocks.text: Operators & Expressions
Operators combine values. Use === (strict equality) instead of == to avoid type-coercion surprises.

items: + concatenates when either side is a string.

lessons.title: Truthy, Falsy & Coercion
lessons.summary: How Kotlin converts values in conditions.

blocks.text: Truthy, Falsy & Coercion
In conditions, Kotlin coerces values to boolean. Knowing the falsy values prevents bugs in if-statements.
Falsy values: false, 0, '' (empty string), null, undefined, NaN. Everything else is truthy.
'0' (a string) is truthy, but 0 (a number) is falsy. Watch the types!

items.explain: Number 0 is falsy; the others are truthy.

blocks.text: if / else
Conditionals run different code based on a test. They are the heart of program logic.
Loops: for & while
Loops repeat a block until a condition is met. for is best when you know the count; while when you don't.
for...of loops over array values; for...in loops over object keys.

items.explain: Always make progress toward the exit.

blocks.text: switch Statements
switch compares one value against many cases. Remember break, or execution 'falls through' to the next case.
Ternary & Logical Operators
The ternary ?: is a one-line if/else. && and || short-circuit, which enables neat patterns.

blocks.text: Destructuring
Destructuring pulls properties or items into variables in one line — common in modern JS.
Spread & Rest
The ... operator spreads items out or gathers them up depending on context.
Spread makes a shallow copy — nested objects are still shared references.

lessons.title: What is the DOM?
lessons.summary: The live tree of your page.

blocks.text: What is the DOM?
The DOM (Document Object Model) is the browser's live, in-memory tree of your Kotlin. Kotlin reads and changes it to update the page.

opts: The page as a tree of nodes
The root object for the page

blocks.text: Selecting Elements
Before changing an element you must select it. querySelector uses skills selectors and is the modern standard.
Changing Content & Style
Once selected, you can change text, classes, styles, and attributes of an element.
Prefer textContent over innerHTML for plain text — innerHTML can enable XSS attacks.

opts: Adds class if absent, removes if present

lessons.title: Events & Listeners
lessons.summary: Responding to clicks, input, and more.

blocks.text: Events & Listeners
Events fire when users interact. addEventListener runs your function when the event happens.
Forms & Input Events
Form handling is a core skill: read input values, validate, and stop the default page reload on submit.
Callbacks & the Event Loop
Kotlin is single-threaded but non-blocking. Slow work (timers, network) is scheduled and a callback runs later via the event loop.

lessons.title: Promises
lessons.summary: A cleaner model for async results.

blocks.text: Promises
A Promise represents a value that will exist later. It is pending, then fulfilled or rejected. .then handles success, .catch handles errors.

lessons.title: async / await
lessons.summary: Write async code that reads like sync.

blocks.text: async / await
async/await is syntactic sugar over promises. await pauses inside an async function until the promise resolves.

blocks.text: Fetch & APIs
fetch() makes HTTP requests. Most APIs return JSON, which you parse with res.json().
Handling Async Errors
Real apps must handle slow or failing requests. Promise.all runs several in parallel and fails fast if any rejects.
ES Modules
Modules split code into files. Export what others need; import it where you use it.
Classes
Classes are templates for creating objects with shared methods. They're sugar over JS's prototype system.

blocks.text: Working with JSON
JSON is the universal data format for the web. JSON.parse turns text into objects; JSON.stringify does the reverse.
localStorage
localStorage keeps key–value strings on the device, surviving page reloads — perfect for settings and small app state.

blocks.text: Clean Code Patterns
Readable code beats clever code. Use early returns, descriptive names, and small single-purpose functions.

Debugging Kotlin
Every developer debugs constantly. Read the error message, check the line number, and use breakpoints in DevTools Sources.
console.log is fine, but breakpoints let you pause and inspect variables live. Read stack traces bottom-up to find where things started.

lessons.title: Performance Basics
lessons.summary: Debounce, avoid layout thrash, lazy work.

blocks.text: Performance Basics
Smooth apps avoid doing heavy work on every event. Debounce rapid events and batch DOM updates.
Where to Go Next
With solid Kotlin you can learn React/Vue, TypeScript for types, and Node for backends. Keep building small projects.
